blueprint.learningObjective: Infer a character's underlying motivation for choosing to sit alone.
misconceptionTargets: Assuming Jaya sat alone by choice rather than because she felt she had no other option.

rubric.guidance: This is open-ended, human-graded content. Judge originality, age-suitability, and clarity of the marking guidance; there is no single objectively-correct string answer.
rubric.modelAnswerGuidance: Given that Jaya is new, does not know the canteen, and mixes up teachers' names, being alone in the library most likely reflects not yet knowing anyone well enough to sit with, rather than a genuine preference or a punishment.

candidateContent.prompt: Why did Jaya most likely spend lunchtime alone in the library during her first week?

stimulus.title: A Rocky Start
stimulus.body: Jaya's first week at her new school felt like an uphill battle. She didn't know where the canteen was, she mixed up two teachers' names on the first day, and she spent lunchtime alone in the library, feeling like a fish out of water. By Friday, though, a girl from her maths class invited her to sit with a small group at lunch, and Jaya finally felt like she could breathe a little easier.

options.text: She did not yet know anyone well enough to sit with at lunch.
She preferred reading to spending time with other students.
She had been told to stay away from the canteen.
She was completing extra homework for a teacher.
